messages:
laura: Heads-up: onboarding folks hit a failing quickstart this morning. The TypeScript sample imports `RedwoodClient` from `@redwood/sdk` but current SDK exports `Redwood` and the method is `text.generate`. Also the example uses `REDWOOD_API_KEY` env var in examples/ts/README.md.

sam: Oof. Is it breaking CI or just local runs?

laura: Both. CI failed the snippet-runner for the TS quickstart. Error: `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor`.

rachel: I can take a look. Likely we updated the SDK API in v1 and the example wasn't updated. Quick patch idea: change import to `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';` and update call to `await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.0', input: '...' })`. Also swap env var to `REDWOOD_KEY`.

sam: Also we should add a one-line compatibility note for customers still on 0.x: show a small snippet labeled "Legacy (0.x)" that uses `createCompletion`. Avoids surprise.

laura: Agreed — keep canonical example current, add a short legacy box. No shims in main path.

alex: Quick lint/formatting thing: the TS example uses `any` and fails `tsc` in strict mode on snippet-runner. I'll patch types and run tests.

rachel: Thanks. I ran a grep and found a few more occurrences: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=` in `examples/*/README.md` and some sample-app env examples.docs-bot: automation: opening follow-up issue to replace deprecated env var names and older API calls across repos.

ci-bot: snippet-runner report: 3 failing snippets in examples repo: ts-quickstart, node-sample-app, and python-snippets (auth mismatch). Logs: https://ci.redwood/artefacts/snippet-runner/1744315555

sam: I'll draft a PR to update the TS quickstart + add legacy note + bump example deps. Will include CHANGELOG entry.

laura: Please also update the Troubleshooting section with a tiny blurb about transient 429s and link to our `withRetries()` helper from `@redwood/devx`. New hires copy the quickstart into prod and then complain about flakiness.

alex: One more gotcha: the sample code shows `client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: '...' })` — combine of wrong param name (`prompt` vs `input`) and wrong model id. I'll fix both.

rachel: For the python snippets, the auth example sets `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in code. We should show env var usage and `os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')`.

sam: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/459 — updates TS quickstart, adds legacy block, fixes env vars, and updates python snippets.

ci-bot: CI run started for PR #459. Note: we require all snippet fences to be annotated with language (```ts, ```py, ```js) or snippet-runner fails.

laura: Good reminder. Add a lint step in CI to catch missing fence languages.

rachel: Minor UX suggestion: include a one-liner in README that points to `examples/compat/README.md` which houses legacy snippets and migration notes. That keeps quickstart clean.

sam: Adding that now. Also adding tests that assert `REDWOOD_KEY` appears in all README files.

laura: Once merged, can someone send a short note on #new-hires so trainers know the fix landed? This blocked onboarding today.

docs-bot: checklist: [x] update TS quickstart snippet [x] replace env var in python snippets [x] add legacy compatibility section [ ] add CI snippet fence lint [ ] create repo-wide replace PR for `REDWOOD_API_KEY` occurrences.

ci-bot: PR #459 passed snippet-runner on second try (fixed fence languages). Ready to merge after maintainers approve.

alex: Merged and bumped examples tag to v0.12.2. I also ran the grep suggested by docs-bot and opened branch with bulk replacements.

laura: Thanks all. I'll update the onboarding checklist and forward the trainers the new quickstart link.
